name: Kronplatz
note: Plan de Corones. One mountain, lifts up from three valleys.
operationsProvenance: PLACEHOLDER. lastUp and queue are not from OpenStreetMap and are not yet from the resort either. They must be replaced with published lift hours before this resort is marked available.
defaultBaseWhy: The Olang gondola is the base most people use and the one OSM names after the village. The other three are found through their lift names.
toleranceWhy: Re-measured after the prune fix. 90 gives 26 of the 32 published lifts, 66.9 km, and a day at every grade from all four bases. 60 keeps more piste on paper but leaves Kronplatz 2000 with nothing for a blue skier and Korer with under two hours at red; 120 costs four kilometres and twenty-seven runs for the same lift count.
publishedSource: Kronplatz's own published network figures, as recorded in src/resorts/index.js before this resort had data.
bboxWhy: Widened south and out to take in St Vigil / San Vigilio and Pfalzen. The old box stopped at 46.71 and three lifts — Miara, Col Toron, Ski Pfalzen — already ran off its edges, which is why the graph held 19 of the 32 lifts the resort publishes.
basesWhy: The village names OSM does not use, plus the lift names it does. Kronplatz's valley stations are nodes called Kronplatz 2000 (Reischach), Korer (Percha) and Miara (St. Vigil), so asking only for the villages found one base out of four and left three car parks unreachable.
baseNamesWhy: The Kronplatz I cable car is the Bruneck base, and 'Kronplatz I' is what OSM and the sign at the bottom both call it. It is not what anyone says when they say where the car is: they say Bruneck, or Brunico. Both, because South Tyrol signs both and a skier may know either.

extraPlaces.name: Rentasport Kronplatz
extraPlaces.note: Seilbahnstraße 12/b — Via Funivia 12/b, 39031 Reischach / Riscone. rentasport.biz and rentandgo.it, read 8 Sep 2026; the shop's own page puts it inside the cable car station, 40 m from the Kronplatz 1-2 lift. No geocoder is reachable from this build, so the coordinate is OpenStreetMap's own Kronplatz I station node (320974326). OSM's address node for the same street number is the K1 restaurant, 51 m away, at the far end of the same building — two readings that agree.

extraPlaces.name: Rentasport Kronplatz Ried-Percha
extraPlaces.note: Via Stazione 2 / Bahnhofstraße 2, at the Ried valley station, 39030 Perca / Percha. rentasport.biz and rentandgo.it, read 8 Sep 2026. The coordinate is OpenStreetMap's Ried station node (1573070001), which is the valley station the address itself names; the export holds no address node for that street, so this is the station rather than the doorway — a hundred metres at the outside.

extraPlaces.name: Rent and Go Olang
extraPlaces.note: Gassl 21, 39030 Olang / Valdaora. sportrent.it and rentandgo.it, read 8 Sep 2026; its own page says a few steps from the cable car. The coordinate is OpenStreetMap's Olang I — Valdaora I station node (283553882), for the same reason as Ried: no address node for Gassl in the export, and no geocoder from the build.

extraPlacesWhy: Places that are real and are not in OpenStreetMap. The export's own hire sweep — anything tagged ski, sport, rental or outdoor, or named rent-and-go, noleggio or verleih — finds six shops at Kronplatz and all six are at St Vigil or San Lorenzo, so Reischach, Olang and Percha, three of the four valleys people park in, had no ski hire on the map at all. These three are the Rent and Go and Rentasport shops at those bases, reported as a gap twice. Every note says where the address was read and what the coordinate actually is, because no geocoder is reachable from the build: a station node with the discrepancy stated is worth more than a street number placed by eye. Shape: {"name": "Rent and Go Olang", "kind": "rental", "lat": 46.74669, "lon": 12.01065, "note": "where you checked it, and when"}. kind is one of hut, restaurant, cafe, rental, parking. The note is required and the build fails without it — see scripts/sources/manual.mjs for why.
